pride_data.title: Structure of the Plant Plastid-Encoded RNA Polymerase
pride_data.projectDescription: In this study, the native Sinapis alba plastid-encoded RNA polymerase (PEP) complex was purified and cross-linking MS was used to help in its structure determination.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Aerial parts of 1-week old Sinapis alba were homogenised in homogenisation buffer [Tris-HCl (10 mM, pH 7.6 at 4 °C), KCl (50 mM), MgCl2 (5 mM), EDTA (2 mM), sorbitol (0.7 M), DTT (1 mM)] using a Waring blender (CB15V) at power 4 for 20 s. Homogenate was filtered through BioDesign cheesecloth (Fisher) and then through three layers of miracloth (Sigma). Chloroplasts were pelleted (4000 x g, 10 min, 4 °C), washed in homogenisation buffer supplemented with BSA (1 g/L), re-centrifuged (3000 x g, 10 min, 4°C) and the pellet was snap-frozen in liquid N2 and stored at -80°C. Plastid pellets from ~2 kg of leaf material was resuspended in 360 mL of lysis buffer [Tris (50 mM, pH 7.6 at 4°C), NaCl (150 mM), MgCl2 (2 mM), CaCl2 (1 mM), ZnCl2 (10 μM), glycerol (10%), DTT (2 mM), Triton X-100 (2%), DNase I (10 μg/mL), Pefabloc (1 mg/mL) (Sigma)] and incubated at 4 °C for 30 min with stirring, clarified (40,000 x g, 30 min, 4 °C) and the supernatant was filtered through a 0.45 μm filter. Clarified chloroplast lysate was loaded onto a HiPrep Heparin FF 16/10 column (Cytiva) in PEP Buffer [Tris (50 mM, pH 7.6 at 4°C), NaCl (150 mM), MgCl2 (2 mM), 10 µM ZnCl2, 10% glycerol, 2 mM DTT]. Elution was with PEP Buffer containing 600 mM NaCl. Eluates were dialysed in PEP buffer for 2 h at 4°C and loaded onto a HiTrap Heparin HP 5 ml column (Cytiva) in PEP Buffer. Elution was with PEP buffer containing NaCl at 600 mM. Eluted peak was loaded onto a HiPrep Sephacryl S-300 HR (26/60) (Cytiva) column in SEC Buffer [Tris (50 mM, pH 7.6 at 4°C), NaCl (200 mM), MgCl2 (2 mM), 10 µM ZnCl2, 5% glycerol, 2 mM DTT].  Fractions from SEC were resolved by SDS-PAGE and presence of RPOB was assessed by immunodetection using anti-RPOB antibody (Agrisera: AS15 2867, used at 1:1000 dilution; secondary antibody was Chicken anti-Rabbit IgG HRP Conjugate, Agrisera: CkxRb 003 EHRPX). Fractions showing a high signal were pooled and loaded onto a Capto HiRes Q 5/50 column (Cytiva) in SEC Buffer. We performed a gradient elution (200–1000 mM NaCl) with 30 column volumes of SEC buffer and monitored absorbance at 280 nm. The first major peak (300–400 mM) was collected and diluted 1:4 in PEP buffer containing 50 mM NaCl and reloaded onto the same column. Pure PEP samples were eluted with SEC buffer containing 650 mM NaCl and buffer-exchanged into PEP buffer containing 50 mM NaCl in a VivaspinTM 500 centrifugal concentrator with a 100 kDa molecular weight cutoff (MWCO). The PEP complex was concentrated ~1 mg/mL.  Purified PEP complex was buffer exchanged into an amine-free buffer (50 mM HEPES, 100 mM NaCl, 2 mM MgCl2, 10 µM ZnCl2, 2 mM DTT, pH 7.5) using ZebaSpin desalting columns (7K MWCO; ThermoFisher Scientific). Crosslinkers disuccinimidyl sulfoxide (DSSO) was prepared in anhydrous DMSO at 10 mM.  and Sulfosuccinimidyl 4,4'-azipentanoate (sulfo-SDA), dihydrazide sulfoxide (DHSO) and 4-(4,6-dimethoxy-1,3,5-triazin-2-yl)-4-methylmorpholinium chloride (DMTMM) were prepared in MillQ water at 10 mM, 25 mM and 25 mM, respectively. For each cross-linking experiment, ~10 µg of the complex at ~0.5 mg/mL was used. Cross-linking was performed either with 1 mM DSSO (45 min incubation), or a combination of 2.5 mM each of DHSO and DMTMM together (2 h incubation), or 1 mM sulfo-SDA (45 min incubation) at 30°C. Post-cross-linking, DSSO and sulfo-SDA reactions were quenched with 100 mM NH4HCO3 at 30°C for 20 min. Excess sulfo-SDA crosslinker was removed using ZebaSpin columns and exposed to 365 nm UV (Penn OC Photoreactor M1; Penn Optical Coatings) for 10 min. Excess DHSO/DMTMM were removed by ZebaSpin columns. All samples were then freeze-dried. Samples were dissolved in 20 μL of 8 M urea, reduced (5 mM DTT, 37 °C, 30 min) and alkylated (10 mM iodoacetamide, 20 min, 25 °C in the dark). Samples were diluted to 6 M urea using 25 mM Tris-HCl pH 8, and Trypsin/Lys-C mix (Promega) was added to an enzyme:substrate ratio of 1:25 (w/w) and incubated at 37 °C for 4 h. Subsequently, urea was diluted to 0.75 M and samples were left at 37 °C overnight (~16 h). Samples were acidified with formic acid to 2% (v/v), centrifuged at 16,000 g for 10 min, desalted using 50-mg Sep-Pak tC18 cartridges (Waters), and eluted in 60:40:0.1 acetonitrile:water:formic acid (v/v/v), and freeze-dried. Peptides were resuspended in 4% (v/v) acetonitrile, 0.1% (v/v) formic acid and loaded onto a 30 cm × 75 µm inner diameter column packed in-house with 1.9 µm C18AQ particles (Dr Maisch GmbH HPLC) using a Dionex UltiMate 3000 UHPLC (ThermoFisher Scientific). Peptides were separated using a linear gradient of 10–50% buffer B over 107 min at 300 nL/min at 55°C (buffer A = 0.1% (v/v) formic acid, buffer B = 80% (v/v) acetonitrile and 0.1% (v/v) formic acid). Mass analyses were performed using a Q-Exactive HF-X mass spectrometer (ThermoFisher Scientific) in data-dependent top 12 mode (MS1, R = 120,000, MS2 = 30,000, stepped NCE = (sulfo-SDA: 24, 28, 32) or (DSSO/DHSO/DMTMM: 21, 27, 33), minimum charge state of +3).
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: All datasets were processed using MaxQuant (v2.4.2). Additionally, the sulfo-SDA and DMTMM datasets were also processed with MS Studio (v2.4.0.3545) and pLINK (v2.3.11), respectively. Generally, the following key parameters were used: peptide mass between 300–10,000 Da, minimum peptide length of 6 residues, precursor mass tolerance ±10 ppm, product-ion mass tolerance of ±20 ppm. Allowable variable modification = oxidation (M), allowable static modification = carbamidomethyl (C), enzyme specificity of Trypsin with up to four missed cleavages (excluding the site of cross-linking), and FDR control at 1%. The search database used was a manually curated database comprising of Sinapis alba plastid-encoded RNA polymerase complex proteins (20 entries). Cross-linked spectral matches from MS Studio were also manually visually assessed.
